Foundation · Scope, grain and definitions

What the data covers, and what OTIF means here

02 / 20

Coverage and grain

Rows × columns50,000 × 30
Grain1 row = 1 order
Date range2026-01-01 → 12-31
Distinct days365 of 365
Customers6,348
Duplicate order IDs0
Missing values1 field only

Volume is flat across the year (4,030–4,319 orders/month) and across weekdays, so period comparisons are like-for-like.

30 columns, five families

  • Order — id, date, value, priority, payment, category, weight, package size
  • Customer — id, segment, city, country
  • Network — warehouse id/city, processing hours, distance
  • Transport — carrier, shipping method, shipping cost, attempts, weather
  • Outcome — promised/actual days, delay, late flag, status, tracking, rating, return + reason

OTIF definition used

An order counts as On-Time In-Full only when all three hold:

  1. On time — actual_delivery_days ≤ promised_delivery_days (the file's late_delivery = No)
  2. First attempt — delivery_attempts = 1
  3. No fulfilment fault — no return for Damaged Package, Wrong Item or Product Defect

The on-time-only and in-full-only rates are shown separately throughout, so the composite can always be audited against its parts.

Network · Sourcing logic

Only three of seventeen markets are actually being sourced

17 / 20

Average route length (km) by destination market and origin node

Teal = shorter than the market average, red = longer. Outline = the row's shortest node.

In-country node vs cross-border, tested

Method: Welch two-sample test on shipping cost, domestic-node orders vs all others, per market with a co-located node. Only Singapore, the UAE and the United States clear p < 0.05. Everywhere else, which warehouse ships the order makes no measurable difference to distance or cost — the assignment is effectively random.

Singapore is the proof of concept: in-country sourcing cuts the route from 3,272 km to 50 km, cost from $162.35 to $17.02, and lifts OTIF from 29% to 56%. Nine other nodes are not doing this job.

Plan · Quantified scenario

A third of the shipping bill is addressable

Three levers applied in sequence to every order, so no dollar is counted twice. Ranked by confidence, not by size.

19 / 20

Baseline to optimised shipping spend

Lever detail and confidence

The fourth lever is free: moving the four weakest carriers' volume to the four strongest adds 8.1pp of OTIF on 24,923 orders at $0.28 less per order. It appears in no waterfall because it costs nothing.

Plan · Next 90 days

What to do, and what this analysis cannot tell you

20 / 20

Sequenced action plan

HorizonActionSuccess measure
Days 0–30Freeze the four weakest carriers on new volume; re-tender their lanes to the top four at the existing rate card.Blended OTIF 34.8% → 38.8% at flat cost
Days 0–30Audit the “International” service tier: confirm whether it is a customs product or a mispriced default, on the 15,839 orders it carried.Written rule for when the tier is mandatory
Days 30–60Re-route Singapore, UAE and US demand to the in-country node; instrument why the other seven nodes never win their home market.$337K annualised; SG route 3,272 → 50 km
Days 30–60Put a hard 24-hour service level on warehouse processing and alert on the tail rather than the mean.18.2% of orders >24h → <5%; +3.4pp OTIF
Days 60–90Introduce a minimum-order or shipping-contribution rule for orders under $25 and consolidate them onto the economy tier.$363K; 11,527 orders currently losing $1.18M
Days 60–90Re-baseline delivery promises on weather-exposed lanes instead of absorbing a 3.2-day average delay in snow.Rating recovery on the 9,904 storm/snow orders

Assumptions and limitations

  • Substitutability is assumed. Standard is observed on every route band including 8,000 km+, so the swap is physically possible — but customs or contractual reasons for the International tier are not in the data and must be checked first.
  • Cost is censored at $500. 658 orders sit on the cap, so long-haul cost — and the long-haul saving — is understated.
  • No product margin in the file. “Drain” compares freight to gross order value, not to contribution. It ranks severity, not P&L truth.
  • Correlation, not causation. Weather, processing time and distance co-move with route type; slide 7 is a decomposition, not an experiment.
  • Scenario savings are static. They hold volume, mix and rates constant and assume no customer response to slower service.
  • 5,816 orders were still open at snapshot; their delay can only grow, so OTIF here is an optimistic bound.
Do the free things first: carrier re-tendering and the 24-hour processing SLA cost nothing and move OTIF by roughly 11 points combined.
